No revenue statement, no product statement, and no description of how ManyChat charges customers were extracted from the document. The evidence establishes only that the company states 140,000+ bots [S1] and 500M messages [S2, S3] as traction metrics (in a slide context headed 'Traction by Apr-16'), and that it operates in software [P2] (current profile, undated) at Series A stage [P1]. Who pays, what they pay, and what drives growth are not found in the extracted evidence. Information Readiness Not assessed. Open Concerns • Ambiguous message-volume measurement bases: The deck states '500M messages' (slide context: 'Traction by Apr-16') [C3/S2] and '500M messages/month' on a separate page [C2/S3]. These cannot be compared without clarification; one or both figures may misrepresent the scale of actual activity. • Unverified funding figure with undated claim: Pitch Deck Hunt lists $23.1M raised [C1, S4], but no date is stated and no external source confirmed the amount. It is unknown whether this reflects cumulative raises, a single round, or a different basis entirely. • Complete absence of financial disclosure: Revenue, burn rate, and use of proceeds are not found in the extracted evidence, making it impossible to understand the financial position or the sustainability of the stated traction. • No problem, product, team, or market disclosure: Six major due-diligence categories — problem statement, market size, revenue model, team, product description, and risk factors — are not found in the extracted evidence, leaving the investment rationale almost entirely unsubstantiated. What Would Change the Picture The single most important missing piece of evidence is audited or accountant-reviewed financial statements showing revenue, gross margin, and monthly burn rate — this would allow an assessment of whether the stated traction (140,000+ bots [S1], 500M messages [S2]) translates into a viable and scalable business, and would provide a basis for evaluating the $23.1M funding figure (per Pitch Deck Hunt) [S4] in context.
